chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

Shall I inform you of something that brings one closer to Allah, closer to Paradise, and farther from the Fire? He said, 'Yes.' He said: 'Adopt generosity, for Allah created His creation with His mercy for His mercy, so He made them worthy of kindness and a place for goodness, and a face for people to strive towards, in order to revive them just as rain revives the arid land. Those are the believers, the secure ones on the Day of Judgment.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual benefit of generosity according to Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elevates generosity (*sakhā'*) from a mere social virtue to a spiritual mechanism for salvation, linking it directly to the divine attribute of mercy. The metaphor of rain reviving barren land underscores the Shia concept of the believer as a source of life and sustenance for the community, a theme deeply resonant with the concept of *Ahl al-Bayt* as the spiritual rain for the world. This narration reinforces the practical implication that true faith is manifested through active benevolence that alleviates the spiritual and material drought of others.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Haroun Bin Muslim, from Mas’ada Bin Sadaqa who said, 
‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said to one of his<sup>asws</sup> gathered ones: ‘Shall I<sup>asws</sup> inform you with some which would take you closer to Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and closer to the Paradise, and remote from the Fire?’ So he said, ‘Yes’.

So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is upon you with the generosity, for Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Created creatures by His<sup>azwj</sup> Mercy for His<sup>azwj</sup> Mercy, so He<sup>azwj</sup> Made them deserving ones for the acts of kindness and a place for goodness, and for the people a direction for them to strive towards them, in order to revive them just as the rain revives the arid land. They (the revivers) are the Believers, the Secured ones on the Day of Judgement’.
en.sarwar: 12. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Harun ibn Muslim from Mas’adah ibn Sadaqah who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, once said to a certain person in his presence, ‘

Should I tell you about something that gets you close to Allah and to paradise and away from hell fire?’ He said, ‘Yes, please do so.’ He (the Imam) then said, ‘You must maintain generosity. Allah has created a creature by His kindness for His kindness. He has made them true deserving recipients of Benevolent Assistance, the proper place for good deeds, and a direction for people to strive toward them, so that they revive them, just as rain revives the barren land. Such people are the believers who live in peace in paradise on the Day of Judgment.’”
